overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the chair did not anticipate the off-notice Fire Department topic 48 hours ahead, and no individual notice to the Fire Chief was required. Conflict-of-interest issues were declined.

allegations.summary: Board discussed a Fire Department topic at its March 19 meeting that was not listed on the posted notice.
allegations.key_passage: we do not find a violation of the Open Meeting Law because a public body may discuss a topic not listed on a meeting notice if the topic was not anticipated by the chair 48 hours in advance of the meeting.

allegations.summary: Board failed to give the Fire Chief individual notice that he would be discussed at the March 19 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Board was not required to notify the Fire Chief that it would be discussing him, the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by failing to provide him with individual notice.

allegations.summary: Complaint raised conflict of interest issues, which the AG declined to review as outside its Open Meeting Law jurisdiction.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review, and offer no opinion on, any conflict of interest issues raised in the complaint, as those matters fall outside the scope of our jurisdiction.
